data.title: HTTP
data.tagline: Send a request and receive a response over the web
data.description: HTTP is the request-response protocol browsers and APIs use. A request includes a method, URL, headers, and sometimes a body; the response includes a status, headers, and content. Methods and status codes should match what actually happened.

use: Describe success, redirects, client errors, and server errors
avoid: Use a successful status code for a failed operation
Change data with a request intended only for reading
Retry every failed request without limits
Log sensitive headers or bodies carelessly

explanation.title: HTTP vs HTTPS: what is the difference?
explanation.text: Use HTTPS for public sites and production APIs. It keeps HTTP's request-response rules while TLS protects the connection. What it is: HTTP — The standard request-and-response rules between client and server.; HTTPS — Standard HTTP traffic carried over an encrypted TLS connection.. Data in transit: HTTP — Plain text; network observers along the path can read or modify data.; HTTPS — Encrypted in transit; protected from eavesdropping and silent tampering.. When to use: HTTP — Local development and offline testing (e.g., http://localhost).; HTTPS — Public deployments, user authentication, payments, and production APIs.. Submitting a production login form: Over plain HTTP, network devices along the route may read the password. HTTPS encrypts the connection and verifies the server's identity, but it cannot fix server vulnerabilities or replace authorization and input validation.

lessonPractice.title: After changing a nickname, the page does not update and Network shows POST /profile returned 400. What should be checked next?

options.label: Inspect what the request sent and what the 400 response specifically reports
options.feedback: HTTP exposes the actual request and response. A 400 means the request was not accepted, so the evidence comes first.

options.label: Use the 400 status to show 'Network error' without reading the request or response
options.feedback: A 400 means the server received but rejected the request. Ignoring details loses actionable field or format evidence.

options.label: Change POST to GET, put the nickname in the URL, and send it again
options.feedback: A save should follow the API contract. Changing the method alters semantics without explaining the rejection.

data.agentPrompt: Saving the nickname returns 400. Inspect the actual method, URL, body, and response, identify why the server rejected it, then make the smallest fix. Do not reduce it to a generic network error or change methods arbitrarily. Resend and confirm the successful result.
